name: Patchwork Collective Prodigy's Oversized Hand-Me-Down Set
description: An enormous adult-sized Halversen synth-wool sweater, three sizes too big, with the sleeves rolled up eight times and a crude BCI port cutout hacked into the neckline with scissors — the kid did it themselves. Beneath it, children's leggings in mismatched patterns and scuffed canvas shoes with the toes written on in permanent marker. A battered satchel worn crossbody is filled, visibly, with salvaged data chips and a cracked tablet.
functionality: Self-modified BCI port cutout allows direct neural interface access; oversized sweater provides warmth well beyond its intended use.
what_it_says: A child who is smarter than everyone around them and has no one making sure they eat.
manufacturer: Halversen (sweater, adult size); everything else scavenged
story_hooks: The data chips in the satchel contain something that multiple factions are currently looking for — the kid has no idea what they found.
The sweater belonged to a parent who hasn't come home in six weeks.

physical_description.visual_profile: A child drowning in oversized adult luxury, transformed into resourceful street wear. The massive Halversen sweater dominates the silhouette, creating a deliberately oversized, almost costume-like effect. Sleeves bunched and rolled repeatedly at the wrists expose forearms. The self-made BCI port cutout at the neckline—rough, uneven scissor marks visible—marks this as a Tier 5 modification of Tier 2 goods. Layered beneath are mismatched children's leggings creating visual discord. The overall impression: intelligent salvage culture, not poverty cosplay.
physical_description.fit: Radically oversized and intentionally so. Sweater hangs to mid-thigh, sleeves rolled 8+ times to functional wrist length. Leggings fitted normally beneath, creating contrast. Canvas shoes slightly worn at heel and toe. The fit hierarchy signals adaptation and ingenuity rather than proper tailoring.
physical_description.primary_material: Halversen synth-wool (sweater—premium thermal-regulating blend); cotton-blend children's leggings (printed patterns faded); scuffed canvas/rubber hybrid shoes; worn cordura shoulder satchel
physical_description.texture: Sweater: soft, lustrous synth-wool with slight pilling at stress points from re-use. Neckline BCI port cutout shows raw, frayed edges where scissors breached the weave. Leggings: worn cotton with visible pilling and fading on thighs/knees. Shoes: canvas scuffed white at toe caps, rubber sole showing wear patterns. Satchel: cracked cordura with visible stitching repairs.
physical_description.color_scheme: Sweater: muted charcoal gray (Halversen signature). Leggings: clashing patterns—one leg neon geometric grid, other rust-colored stripe print, both faded and worn. Shoes: original white canvas, now cream-stained, with permanent marker doodles in blue and red. Satchel: faded olive-drab.
physical_description.closures: Sweater: standard knit—no closure needed. Leggings: elastic waistband (slightly loose, held by drawstring). Shoes: canvas slip-on style, no laces. Satchel: magnetic closure flap, visibly strained.
distinctive_features: Crude BCI port cutout at neckline—self-inflicted scissor work, unfinished edges
Sleeves rolled 8+ times, creating thick cuffs and visual bulk
Permanent marker doodles on shoe toe caps (child's handwriting, data symbols, faces)
Visible interior of satchel crammed with salvaged data chips and cracked tablet screen
Worn crossbody satchel strap, showing stress creasing
Mismatched legging patterns indicating scavenged wardrobe
Pilling and wear on sweater elbows from heavy use
physical_description.tier_indicator: Hybrid Tier 2/Tier 5: Halversen sweater signals wealth (Tier 1-2 retail), but context of oversizing, modification, and pairing with salvage indicates Tier 5 street collective. A child wearing hand-me-downs as power statement.
physical_description.cultural_context: Patchwork Collective member—likely a data scavenger or salvage courier. The BCI port cutout suggests either amateur neural-interfacing ambitions or a joke among peers. Wearing adult luxury modified as street gear communicates: I take what systems discard and make it mine. Wearing Halversen ironically or genuinely unaware of its cost—either way, it's been claimed.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn but not destroyed. Sweater shows gentle signs of being loved and re-used (minor pilling, soft hand). Leggings are visibly faded and tired. Shoes show honest scuff marks, not intentional distressing. Everything functional. The BCI cutout is recent and crude—done with urgency, not care. Satchel is battered but serviceable, with visible repairs suggesting it's been through multiple owners.

image_prompt: A Tier 5 street kid wearing an absurdly oversized charcoal Halversen synth-wool sweater with sleeves rolled 8 times, neckline hacked with a crude scissor-cut BCI port, standing against a rain-slicked GLMZ underpass wall covered in faded tech graffiti and QR decay. Mismatched neon-geometric and rust-stripe leggings visible beneath. Scuffed white canvas shoes with blue permanent-marker doodles. A battered olive cordura satchel worn crossbody, overflowing with visible salvaged data chips and a cracked tablet. Moody cyan and amber neon backlighting from vending machines. Wet concrete reflections. Fashion editorial style, slight grain, desaturated but neon-punchy. Character close-up, 3/4 pose. --ar 2:3 --v 6
